chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ali ibn Muhammad, who reported it to Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abi Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah, 'May I be sacrificed for you, when will the relief come?' He replied, 'O Aba Basir, are you among those who desire this world? Whoever understands this matter has already found relief by awaiting it.'

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The worldly life, often contrasted with the hereafter or spiritual reality.
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: The matter, specifically referring to the Imamate or the divine authority/affair of God.
key_terms.الْغَيْبَةُ: Occultation (implied context), the state of the Imam being hidden from public view.
key_terms.الْفَرَجُ: Relief, deliverance, or opening of affairs, often referring to the appearance of the Imam or spiritual liberation.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'al-Faraj' (relief) in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the concept of 'al-Faraj' from a mere eschatological event to an immediate spiritual state achieved through *intizar* (expectant waiting) and correct doctrinal understanding. This narration underscores the Shia principle that true deliverance begins with the heart's orientation toward the Imam, distinguishing those anchored in faith from those consumed by worldly distractions. It highlights the transformative power of conscious anticipation as a means of spiritual liberation in the present moment.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: 3. Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ali ibn Muhammad, who reported it to Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abi Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah, "May I be sacrificed for you, when will the relief (al-Faraj) come?" He replied, "O Aba Basir, are you among those who desire this world? Whoever understands this matter has already found relief by awaiting it."
